## What Initiative 86 Would Do

Initiative 86, or the Prohibiting Force-Feeding of Birds Act of 2026, would prohibit the practice of force-feeding birds and ban the sale or distribution of any product resulting from force-feeding a bird, including foie gras. Violations would result in fines ranging from $1,000 to $5,000 per violation and the possibility of a business license suspension or revocation.

## Campaign Background

Pro-Animal D.C., a local campaign arm of the national organization Pro-Animal Future, led the petition drive, with activists having worked on getting foie gras out of the city for over four years, first trying the D.C. Election officials confirmed 31,726 valid signatures, which was well above the 23,940 signatures required to place the initiative before voters.

## Restaurant Industry Opposition

The Restaurant Association of Metropolitan Washington did not come out in full opposition, stating in a message that it recognizes people have differing views on foie gras, but a citywide ban is a significant response to a product served by a relatively small number of restaurants.

The most prominent opponent is Bart Hutchins, chef and owner of Butterworth's, an upscale restaurant near Capitol Hill, who uses foie gras in his tartare presentation, to mount sauces, as a pâté, and even for ice cream.
